newsitem.title: KENYA: Sugar ship waiting at Mombasa for lack of document.
newsitem.headline: Sugar ship waiting at Mombasa for lack of document.

text.p: A ship carrying 5,000 tonnes of sugar from Sudan has been denied berthing facilities at the Kenyan port of Mombasa because its officials have failed to produce its original bill of lading, port sources said.

They told Reuters on Friday that the ship, the MV Kutusovo, had been lying midstream since February 20 when it arrived in Mombasa from Port Sudan. Kenyan officials had said it would not discharge its cargo without the correct papers.

A spokesman for the ship's agents, Mitchell Cotts, told Reuters the ship faced another major problem -- the port's warehouses, where the sugar was meant to be stored, were filled with chemicals and other equipment.
The spokesman said the ship's bill of lading had arrived on Tuesday but storage posed a major problem and the Kutusovo would remain midstream for another two to five days.
He said part of the consignment was in transit but some would be offloaded for the local Kenyan market.
Most sugar arriving at the Mombasa port is normally in transit to Uganda and Rwanda but Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi has repeatedly said some got into the Kenyan market.
"We shall monitor the movement of this sugar once it is offloaded," a senior customs official said.
